doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: How Hey gets an assignment: cassettes and lead sheets
summary: Hey has perfect pitch and usually gets only a cassette of the song, listening closely to the whole track before writing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well I want to fast forward a little bit and really try to get into your thinking about when you got an assignment, a commission to write horn parts for a specific record, I think I read that first of all you have perfect pitch, is that correct?
So when you got a lead sheet — what did they give you? What did their producer give you and did you pay attention to it?

Almost in every case all I got was, well back then a cassette. You know Quincy, David Foster or any of these things, they would send me a cassette of the song. That’s it. If I ever got a lead sheet –- which was rare — I never looked at it because by the time the lead sheet — I did it in the beginning. Okay the guy sent me the lead sheet, usually just kind of rough chords, and I figured out that okay they repeated that and then they cut out these bars the next time and then they did this the next. You know it was like more work to look at their lead sheet than for me to take five minutes and write out a chart — a rough chart. And then with that, you know just kind of a pencil sketch of the tune, I would intensely listen to the song. I mean that’s one of the better things that I think I do is listen to what they’re giving me. Because that’s going to stay. My horn parts, if I write some horn parts, they’re not necessarily going to stay. But this is the rock for them, and I’m just going to be on top of that. So I have to know exactly what they like and what’s there so I would know every keyboard voicing, all the guitar parts, the bass part, the drum fills. I would know all of that stuff and know where the vocal is that I shouldn’t be. So that was kind of the modus of how I would write horn parts is start with all of that and listen to the song and then where does anything need to be.
